full_judgment:
These two Civil Revision Cases have arisen out of two orders passed on two different dates by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court Dhaka in Title Suit No. 21 of 1993. The Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 482 of 1993 on 22.2.93 at the instance of defendant No. 8 K. M. Sarwar Hossain is directed against the order passed on 16.2.1993 rejecting his application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the Rule issued in the other Revision Case No. 713 of 1993 at the instance of the plaintiff Kazi Mosharraf Hossain is directed against the order passed on 24.2.1993 rejecting his prayer for temporary injunction and thereby vacating the ad-interim injunction issued earlier, Both the cases are being disposed of by this judgment and order. 

 2. The above mentioned suit was filed for declaration that discharge by defendant Nos. 2 to 18 of any function as office-bearers of the Central Committee of Bangladesh Pustak Prakashak and Bikreta Samity (Bangladesh Book Publishers and Book Sellers Association) and holding of meetings of the said Committee scheduled on 11.2.1993 and 17.2.1993 by defendant No. 9 vide his notice dated 4.2.1993 were illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff, as well as for permanent injunction restraining defendant No. 1 from declaring the result of the election of the office-bearers held on 4.12.1992 and also restraining the defendants Nos. 12 to 18 from performing any function of the samity as its office-bearers and so on. 

 Briefly stated, the plaintiffs case is that the Bangladesh Pustak Prakashak and Bikreta Samity, briefly the Samity, with its central office at 3, Liakat Avenue under PS Sutrapur within Dhaka city and branches all over Bangladesh was incorporated on 21.11.1981 under the Companies Act. Under Article 25 of the Articles of Association the office-bearers and members of the Central Office and of the Branches are to be elected every two years and such elections are to be held by the Election Commission according to rules framed by the Samity. The result of election is to be announced at a meeting of all members within 30 days of the election. There is provision for an Election Appeal Committee for deciding election disputes. The Election Commission was formed under the Rules and its Chairman issued on 15.10.1992 the schedule of General Election, 1992 to be held on 4.12.1992 in 74 election centres. The election was held on the due date at all the centres, but there were allegations of violation of election rules, rigging and corrupt practice adopted by the contesting candidates and their supporters. There were appeals filed before the Election Appeal Committee challenging the election held in 29 centres, The committee however decided the disputes on 29.12.1992 setting aside elections held in 19 centres only. Notwithstanding the decision of the Appeal Committee and before holding fresh election at the 19 centres some interested persons held a meeting on 13.12.92 and declared the impugned election result and issued notice for holding meetings of the samity on 11.2.1993 and 17.2.1993. In such circumstances the plaintiff who was a contesting candidate for chairmanship of the Samity instituted the above mentioned suit on 10.2.1993 for reliefs as mentioned earlier. 

 3. After filing of the suit on the same date the plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction restraining the defendants in terms of the prayer for permanent injunction as aforesaid. On the next following day i.e. on 11.2.1993, the learned Assistant Judge directed issue of notice upon the defendants to show cause within seven days and also made an order for issue of ad-interim injunction. On 15.2.1993 defendant No. 8 KM Sarwar Hossain filed an application under Order 7 rule 11(d) for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the court had no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the suit, of which the cause of action arose in the head office of the samity lying within the territorial jurisdiction of the local 6th Court of Assistant Judge. The learned Judge heard both sides and by his order dated 16.2.1993 rejected the prayer agreeing with the plaintiff's learned Advocate that defendant Nos. 9 and 12 to 17 ordinarily resided within Kotwali PS i.e. within local jurisdiction of the Court concerned. Challenging this order defendant No. 8 obtained the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 482 of 1993. 

 4. On 18.2.1993 defendant No. 5 Mosharraf Uddin Bhuiyan filed written objection in response to the show cause notice issued upon the defendants by tote learned Judge. The temporary injunction matter was heard on 24.2.1993. The learned Assistant Judge found that the plaintiff had prima facie case to go to trial but that there was no possibility of his suffering any irreparable injury if the injunction was not issued and that the balance of convenience and inconvenience was in favour of the defendants. He accordingly rejected the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction and vacated the order of ad-interim injunction issued by him on 11.2.1993. Challenging this order 'the plaintiff obtained the Rule in Civil Revision 'No. 713 of 1993. 

 5. It has been urged by Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate for the defendants, that defendant Nos. 12 to 17, who are ordinary residents of different places outside Dhaka District, have been falsely shown in the plaint to be residing under the care of defendant No. 9 and no leave of the court having been obtained before institution of the suit is barred by section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submits that before institution of the instant suit the plaintiff brought another suit being Title Suit No. 2 of 1993 in the 6th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka against the same defendants on the same cause of action and praying for self-same relief but that as his prayer for temporary injunction was rejected by that court he brought the instant suit in a different Court. According to him, this subsequently filed suit is an, abuse of the process of the Court and the court can in exercise of its inherent power reject the plaint on this ground as rule 11 of Order 7 CPC is not exhaustive. Mr. SR Pal, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff, on the other hand, submits that in disposing of an application under Order 7 rule 11(d) the court cannot travel beyond the plaint. Referring to the case of Narayan Sankar Vs. Secretary of State for India reported in 30 Bombay 570 he submits that it is not necessary that the leave of the Court must have been obtained before the institution of the suit under section 20(b) and in the reported case the High Court upheld the order under which the leave was given after the framing of the issues. On the question of temporary injunction, Mr. Pal contends that the learned judge has committed an error of law in not holding that the plaintiff would suffer irreparable injury if the part-result of the election is declared before election in the remaining 19 centres are held and that there was no reason for the defendants being in any manner inconvenienced if arrangements are made for entering office after declaration of the overall result of the election of all the 74 centres. Mr. Pal has also drawn my attention to paragraph 14 of the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the contesting defendant opposite party Serajul Hoque wherefrom it is clear that the learned Assistant Judge passed the impugned order dated 24.2.1993 with a clear knowledge of the order of stay of his proceedings granted by this court on 22.2.1993 in Civil Revision No. 482 of 1993 In the affidavit it is stated that the order of this Court was communicated in open court and the learned Court continued with the hearing of the injunction as by then the order officially was not communicated to the Court nor any petition was filed by them". Referring to the decision in the case of Rani Harsamukhi Sinha Vs. Moharaja Sashi Kanta Acharjee, 7 DLR 473 Mr. Pal submits that the impugned order dated 24.2.1993 is not only invalid and irregular but also void ab initio and is therefore liable to be set aside. Title suit No. 2 of 1993 has already been dismissed for non-prosecution on 22.2.1993, he adds. In reply Mr. Asrarul Hossain contends that the impugned order dated 24.2.1993 is an appealable order and as such the revision against the order is incompetent. From the lower Court record he draws attention to the fact that the stay order passed by this Court on 22.2.1993 was brought to the notice of the lower Court on 25.2.1993 by the plaintiff by filing a petition. He has also referred to three decisions in the case of Ramkissen Das Dhanaka and ors. Vs. Satya Charan Law and ors. 50 CWN 310, Ramkumar Poidar Vs. Sholapur Spinning and Weaving Co. Limited AIR 1934 (Bombay) 427, and Bharat Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Kanhaya Lal Guaba AIR 35 (Lahore) 792 and maintained that the internal management of the samity need not be interfered with by an order of injunction. 

 6. Undisputedly the area falling under PS Sutrapur and that falling under PS Kotwali both within Dhaka City fall under the local jurisdiction of the 6th Court and the 3rd Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka respectively. It is also not disputed that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 2 of 1993 in the 6th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka against the defendants for the self-same relief on the same cause of action which arose in the Samity's central office under Sutrapur PS and that the plaintiff failed to obtain injunction in that suit from that Court, where after the instant Suit being Title Suit No. 21 of 1993 was instituted in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge. 

 8. Now the point as regards the abuse of process of the Court as raised by Mr. Hossain invoking inherent jurisdiction of the Court for rejection of plaint. That so far as the question of rejection of the plaint is concerned Order 7 rule 11 is not exhaustive, is now well-settled, and the authority is not wanting in support of the principle that the court in exercise of its inherent power can reject the plaint in an appropriate case. Institution of and proceeding with the subsequently filed instant suit by the same plaintiff against the same set of defendants for the same reliefs on the same cause of action during pendency of the previous suit in a different court is clearly an abuse of the process of the court. The move is all the more reprehensible when the plaintiff after having failed to obtain an order of injunction in the earlier suit brings the later suit and prays for injunction and gets ad interim injunction suppressing the facts that he had the other suit in another court which had refused to grant injunction. It is no valid plea that both the Courts have jurisdiction to entertain the suit or that the earlier suit had been subsequently allowed to be dismissed which was so done after obtaining the injunction in the later suit. The plaintiff's malafides are apparent, and it is a case not only of multiplicity of proceedings but also of clear fraud practised upon the Court. Fraud vitiates the entire proceeding and as such the suit must be held to be not permitted by necessary implications of law. The litigant cannot be rewarded by maintaining the suit on the file in whatsoever manner he pleads the justness of his cause, and it is the duty of the court in exercise of its inherent power to bury the suit the moment such fraud comes to its notice. The plaintiff cannot be allowed to derive any benefit out of his fraudulent acts. It appears that in the defendant's application under Order 7 rule 11 there was reference to the earlier suit and the learned Assistant Judge did not take notice of this. He has failed to exercise his judicial discretion properly and has thereby committed an error of law resulting in error in his decision occasioning failure of justice, in not rejecting the plaint. The impugned order refusing to reject plaint of the suit is therefore liable to be set aside. 

 9. In view of the order which I am going to pass allowing the defendant's prayer for rejection of the plaint any discussion of finding upon the temporary injunction matter would be merely academic, although I must say that on the very admission of the contesting opposite party defendant the impugned order rejecting the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction appears to have been passed by the learned judge after it was brought to his notice from the Bar, though verbally, that the proceedings before him had already been stayed by this Court. In view of the decisions reported in 7 DLR 473 and 7 DLR 82 the order passed by the lower court with knowledge of the stay order passed by this Court is a nullity and void ab initio whatever that may be, if the suit itself goes out of the file there is no question of considering the legality and propriety of the order passed in the suit.
